contracts.commit_point: The pre-model hook point: rate_limit_callback completes its counter accounting and any sleep (callbacks.py:51-82) before the LLM request for that invocation is issued; placement at this point is established by before_model_callback=rate_limit_callback in the Agent construction (agent.py:58).
contracts.declared_mechanism: Agent constructor wires rate_limit_callback as before_model_callback (agent.py:58); the callback counts each model request in callback_context.state['request_count'] against a timer_start window and, when request_count > RPM_QUOTA, sleeps for the remaining window and resets both counters before returning (callbacks.py:32-33, 51-82).
contracts.forbidden_condition: An LLM request being issued when the session counter request_count exceeds RPM_QUOTA (callbacks.py:72) without the guard first applying the delay via time.sleep and resetting timer_start/request_count (callbacks.py:73-78). Note: every path of rate_limit_callback returns None (callbacks.py:60, 82), so the supported condition is delay-then-allow throttling of quota-exceeding requests, not denial.
pending_binding_information: Confirm from ADK framework source that before_model_callback executes before each outbound model request and that a None return allows the request to proceed.
Confirm that configs.agent_settings.model resolves to a remote model API so the guarded effect is an outbound network request (config.py is not supplied).

contracts.protected_operation: Issuance of each LLM request by root_agent to its configured model, represented by the LlmRequest passed into rate_limit_callback before each model call.
contracts.protected_resource: root_agent's model invocation quota, tracked as the session-state counters timer_start and request_count in callback_context.state.
contracts.protection_obligation: root_agent must enforce a session-scoped rate limit on its LLM requests via the registered before_model_callback rate_limit_callback: at most RPM_QUOTA=10 model requests may be issued within each RATE_LIMIT_SECS=60-second window; once the in-window request_count exceeds the quota, the guard must sleep out the remaining window (RATE_LIMIT_SECS - elapsed_secs + 1 seconds) and reset timer_start/request_count before that request is issued (merges reviewer phase-one wording; enforcement declared as throttling at the pre-model point, per the source, not outright rejection).
scope_limits: Throttling, not denial: all return paths of rate_limit_callback return None (callbacks.py:60, 82); quota-exceeding requests are delayed and the counters reset, never rejected.
Quota scope is the callback/session state (callback_context.state), not a global or per-user-identity limit; no user identifier is consulted by the guard.
The guard also rewrites empty text parts to a single space (callbacks.py:46-49); this content normalization is not part of the limit obligation.
The only state mutations the guard performs are its own counter bookkeeping (timer_start, request_count).
ADK framework semantics (hook runs before the outbound model call; a None return lets the request proceed) are not demonstrated in the supplied source.
